title: I created the American Football GM Sim I have wanted to play for decades.
author: Salty_Strike_1714
selftext:
In game screenshots are [HERE](https://imgur.com/a/XbrmClW)

I think this promo does a good job of showing the game's style, humor and potential. But there are so many layers I have been able to build out with Claude. My three development goals at the outset were depth, fun and replayability. I'm astounded by what has been achieved so far and how it will continue to grow.

I have been obsessed with GM sims ever since I was a kid. I'd literally lie in bed at night and interview my players in my head. One summer I even created a Google Doc of their answers, season predictions, everything I could think of (I had a lot of time on my hands).

I always assumed that this type of depth would come to be fully realized in modern games in every sport. It hasn't happened yet. Football Manager has gotten the closest to scratching that itch for me. But even after pouring thousands of hours into that game I still felt as if it was coming up short.

I have spent a ton of money in the past on similar games hoping to find something to fill that void. With the help of Claude I was able to create it.

I am a writer by trade so every writer who covers the league in-game has a backstory, a voice, something they want to say about the sport they love. Interviews can come back to bite you or spur your team on to victory. A college season sims as you progress through yours, and draft analysts will write articles about why a certain prospect is rising or falling. On draft day you might get eviscerated if one of the writers feels you strayed too far from their board. 

There is logic baked into every decision opposing GMs make. Great decisions are praised and poor decisions will have you skewered by a blogger calling for your job. It's a world that feels alive.

You can watch highlights from any game, read breakdowns, or track betting odds. There are weekly MVP Race articles written by a writer who is obsessed with stardom. 

I have created systems for the trade deadline and free agency bidding that keep the league competitive and immersive. Your rivals will literally try to box you out for a star wideout, or a GM you ripped off in the past may refuse to trade you the veteran QB you need. 

Stats remain visible for decades, even centuries, onward. You can sim through a week in a few seconds or spend a weekend dipping into every detail.

I'm really proud of the 3D engine we developed as well. It’s engaging and has a real charm while maintaining the realism that makes every decision feel impactful.

I am hoping to release on Steam in mid/late December.

comments.author: aigamedev-mod
comments.body: u/Salty_Strike_1714 please share some more about how you used AI in developing this. Naming the tools or saying "made with AI" doesn't count. Rule 4 is how we keep promotional posts contributing, by having them talk about the process and how the game was made. Trying to keep the sub focused on dev. This post may be removed if it isn't updated.

replies.author: Rent_South
replies.body: \*wink\* OP :D Its fine, you don' t need to astroturf. Just follow my advice, and make a better promo vid. And you'll have real engagement.

replies.author: Salty_Strike_1714
replies.body: Ha! Thank you. It's good and straightforward advice. This is my first time trying something like this. (As I'm sure is the case with a lot of people right now.)

comments.author: Rent_South
comments.body:
My only advice to you. Is that, in my opinion, you over estimate the feels and vibe that the promo video on this post really conveys. In my honest opinion, it does a huge disservice to your game. Because the graphics and motion/animatons are really underwhelming, the humor you mentioned is just not palpable \*at all\*. I'm sorry if this seems harsh, I wasn't going to comment anything, after checking the video but I checked your actual "in game images" on your imgur link, and these, in my opinion are \*much\* more interesting, and show potential for an intersting GM simulation. 

In my opinion, drop the flluff on the video. Just show the simulation/tactical screen and features, with some brief cuts to the most interesting parts of the promo video (definitely \*not\* the evergreen joke). Most interesting parts of the promo video are:   
\- the throw at 0:44  
\- the double juke at 1:29  
\- ANd you can eventually end the video with the 1:36 celebration. 

Everything else, should \*not\* be used in its current state.

Best of luck.

comments.author: CodeGuyJay
comments.body: Honestly if you’re gonna promote something, leave out how long you worked on it. 10 days and 250 prompts is literally nothing. If your game has all this content and depth, and it was rushed out in ten days it makes me wonder how well thought out it actually is.

replies.author: Salty_Strike_1714
replies.body: Totally fair. To be clear it's not released yet or in a state to be released yet. I'm proud and impressed with its progress.

replies.author: CodeGuyJay
replies.body:
It’s cool to be excited and want to share, but there’s a really big tendency for first time game developers using AI to bite off more than they can chew and overload their game with mechanics/content. Claude makes it so easy to add more, and never says no to adding another feature (or ten).

It’s possible your game is great, I hope it is. The more good AI games that get launched the more we can influence the opinion that all AI is slop. But when you do launch id be really careful about sharing how long you worked on it. Ten days isn’t very long, but neither is six weeks for a game.

replies.author: Salty_Strike_1714
replies.body:
Thank you. The game engine really is a small part of the game, but it's obviously the most visually impressive. The majority of the game is a text based GM sim.  While the time put in and iterations might not be massive there are features in this game that I have wanted to see in Madden for decades. 

That's something I didn't think was possible two weeks ago and I don't see anything similar on the market.

Next time I post I'll highlight the other not so flashy features that give the game, in my opinion, it's staying power.
